text: What if you tried to sleep with 100 women in a single day? First, the math. A day has 1,440 minutes. Divide that by 100, and you get just 14 minutes per woman. No sleep. No food. No breaks. Woman number 1? Easy. But the moment you finish, your body slams on the brakes. It's called the refractory period, and it can last anywhere from a few minutes to a whole day. Scientists still argue about what causes it. So by woman number 5, you're already way behind schedule. Then, the tank starts running dry. Every round drains your sperm reserves, and refilling them takes days. Meanwhile, each round burns about 100 calories and can push your heart to around 130 beats per minute. Every 14 minutes. All day long. But the real danger isn't exhaustion. On any given day, about 1 in 5 Americans has a sexually transmitted infection. Line up 100 people, and that's roughly 20 of them. So how far would you actually get? For most men, a handful. Maybe less. The other 90-something women go home. And you? You sleep for a very, very long time.
